scope: Bounded nearest-prior verification for Gaussian/Theory/A1_2.md, emphasizing NN-native scattering matrices, graph/message-passing solvers, T-matrix neural hybrids, and passive/reciprocal local blocks.

retrieval.retry_policy: No rate-limit retries; fallback to primary publisher, arXiv, institutional, PMC, PubMed, and author-hosted sources under existing user authorization.
retrieval.limitation: Not an exhaustive database search; absence claims are not novelty proof.

claims.claim: A 2023 method combines domain decomposition, generalized scattering matrices, cascaded two-port networks, and Hermite-Gaussian boundary coefficients for radiowave propagation.
claims.risk: It is a forward propagation/domain-decomposition method, not adaptive inverse material Gaussian splatting.

claims.claim: Measured scattered data were transformed into a T-matrix and SVD separated radiating and nonradiating currents before dielectric reconstruction.
T-matrix inversion combined with SOM was used for simultaneous dielectric and PEC reconstruction.
claims.risk: The prior uses mesh subunits and multipole truncation; a Gaussian implementation must distinguish its parameterization and adaptive-order logic.

claims.claim: T-matrix inverse models have already been combined with learned image refinement and with CSI-inspired alternating neural updates.
claims.risk: Song is explicitly a terminal attention-pix2pix/U-Net refinement; Zhang is a deeper alternating physics-inspired hybrid.

claims.a12_anchor: user direction: NN-native rather than terminal U-Net
claims.claim: GNN-based learned iterative full-wave EM solvers already exist.
claims.risk: The broad novelty claim is occupied; Gaussian local modal blocks, inverse de-embedding, and adaptive topology remain the relevant differentiators.

claims.claim: Prior work has represented interacting physical scatterers/particles as graph nodes with physics-aware interaction edges.
claims.risk: These works predict aggregate optical responses rather than composable node-local T/S blocks, but they occupy particle-graph framing.

claims.claim: Neural networks have previously predicted general scattering matrices and learned causal/passive S-parameters.
claims.risk: Jing's conservation/reciprocity is empirical and was not hard-constrained; Torun enforces causality/passivity; Lilja provides structural energy/causality guarantees. These evidence strengths must not be conflated.

claims.a12_anchor: section 26, equations S^H S <= I and S^T = S
claims.claim: Simple unitarity/symmetry formulas require the correct port basis and normalization; evanescent/vector channels obey more general constraints.
claims.risk: A naive Euclidean projection to symmetric contractive matrices may impose the wrong reciprocity metric for truncated Gaussian/Hermite ports.

claims.claim: A recent RF-imaging model already uses a graph-attention backbone but still relies on a U-Net head for the final image.
claims.risk: Merely inserting a GNN before an image decoder would not establish an NN-native scatter-network distinction.

claims.claim: No paper was found in this bounded search that combines adaptive movable/splittable Gaussian material primitives, learned node-local modal T/S blocks, translation-coupled multiple scattering, observable/dark de-embedding, and inverse-driven feature/model-order growth.
claims.risk: Semantic Scholar was rate-limited; the result is a candidate gap, not a novelty proof. Repeat a database-complete search before submission.
